subject: Private VPC: control-plane / data-path attenuation and observability readout
body:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgeworks.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment checklist — observed attenuation on prod-like traffic

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We ran the controlled traffic sweep today against the on-prem staging pod and saw intermittent token-level latency spikes (90th p50 -> 120ms; p90 -> 520ms) when the data-plane passed through the tenant egress proxy. The control-plane signals were steady, but the KV cache hit ratio dropped at the exact times of the spikes.

I've attached a short pcap of the sample window and the observability matrix snapshot. Can you confirm whether this is likely a control-plane coordination issue (authz/signalling) or a data-path batching/caching attenuation? EdgeWorks needs this clarified before we sign-off on the staged cutover.

Attachments: edgeworks-traffic-capture.pcap, observability-matrix-v1.pdf

—Priya
Priya Shah
Platform Engineer, EdgeWorks
priya.shah@edgeworks.io

----

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgeworks.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2027 12:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment checklist — observed attenuation on prod-like traffic

Priya —

Appreciate the quick capture. Short answer: likely both, but the window in the pcap points to an interplay where data-plane egress queuing and KV cache rehydration amplify latency under certain request patterns. Control-plane telemetry stayed healthy, which rules out auth failures, but the control-plane did trigger more frequent small metadata syncs in that interval.

Plan:
- We're going to reproduce against a staging pod with identical network egress (proxy + NAT rules).
- Marissa will run the workload with instrumentation that captures batch sizes and cache TTL expirations.
- Kimberly will validate whether the egress proxy is re-prioritizing small control messages during bursts.

I'll send an ops readout by EOD tomorrow.

Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

----

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgeworks.io>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 22 Jan 2027 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment checklist — observed attenuation on prod-like traffic

Quick status update: I re-ran the sweep in our colo staging with an identical proxy config (iptables + haproxy), captured KV cache metrics, and correlated them to our batching traces. Findings:

- The spikes align with cache rehydration windows when TTLs expire concurrently for hot prefixes (we saw 15–25% concurrent misses).
- When the egress proxy drops packets or retransmits small control frames due to aggressive conntrack timeouts, we see backpressure at the request queue which increases observed batch sizes on the far side of the proxy. Larger batches -> longer tail latency for single-client flows.

Attached: observability-matrix-v1.pdf (annotated) — I added a column that maps the pcap indices to cache miss events.

Next actions I recommend:
1) Short term: tune conntrack/keepalive and increase KV cache TTL jitter to avoid synchronized expirations.
2) Mid term: add a lightweight control-plane heartbeat that will avoid synchronous metadata syncs when the proxy OOS events are frequent.
3) Long term: add an egress QoS policy that favors small control messages over bulk KV prefetch to avoid re-prioritization.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

----

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgeworks.io>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment checklist — observed attenuation on prod-like traffic

Thanks Marissa. I validated the proxy's behavior: the haproxy config had an old default for connection reuse and the kernel's conntrack_active_timeout was low for our policy. I pushed a small patch on the staging config to:
- increase conntrack timeout to 120s for tenant flows
- enable tcp_user_timeout adjustments for keepalive
- add a minimal haproxy map that pins control channels to higher-priority queues

I also prepared a small runbook diff (runbook-delta.patch) that documents these steps and the rollout checklist for customer staging. If we agree on the quick fixes, we can schedule a controlled cutover for EdgeWorks next Tuesday.

Kimberly Park
Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

----

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgeworks.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 16:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment checklist — control-plane / data-path attenuation and observability readout

Priya —

Summary and recommended short-term mitigations (attached artifacts and links below):

- Root cause: synchronized KV cache expirations for hot prefixes + egress proxy conntrack/queueing behavior produced transient backpressure. Control-plane remained nominal; the increased metadata sync frequency is symptomatic, not causal.

- Short-term mitigations (we propose to apply in staging first):
  * Increase KV cache TTL jitter to 60–120s randomization for hot prefixes.
  * Tune conntrack and tcp_user_timeout values on the proxy hosts (patch provided).
  * Apply haproxy priority map for control channels to avoid reordering under burst load.

- Observability changes we will push before cutover:
  * Add a KV miss-rate alert (p90) and a control-plane sync-frequency time series to the customer dashboard.
  * Add trace tags to mark proxy retransmit windows and correlate with batch size histograms.

Attachments: runbook-delta.patch, observability-matrix-v1.pdf
Related evidence: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-edgeworks-vpc-evidence, JIRA INF-4821

If EdgeWorks agrees we'll schedule the staging roll on Tue 02 Feb 2027 and a follow-up validation window. Priya — can you confirm the Tue timeslot (we'll keep a 90-minute validation window)?

Thanks,
Jonas
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
